overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a committee member's email to a quorum did not constitute deliberation because it restated earlier views, and the specific notice was adequate; generalized notice complaints were declined.

allegations.summary: A committee member's September 2021 email with recommendations on a proposed zoning bylaw, sent to a quorum of the committee, allegedly was deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, we find that the email simply memorialized the opinions that Ms. Connolly had previously shared during a Committee meeting held on September 9, 2021, and a Planning Board meeting held on September 13, 2021, and did not convey any new opinions.

allegations.summary: The complaint suggested that the committee's meeting notices generally lack sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: We will not conduct broad audits of a public body and thus decline to review generalized allegations about the notice posting practices of the Committee.

allegations.summary: Whether the September 9, 2021 meeting notice was specific enough to cover the proposed Downtown District Zoning Bylaw.
allegations.key_passage: we have reviewed the notice for the Committee meeting held on September 9, 2021, and find that the notice included sufficient specificity to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting, including a discussion of the proposed Downtown District Zoning Bylaw.
